label: code_review
text:
The loop bound includes `arr.length`, so the last step adds `undefined` and the sum becomes `NaN`. The function therefore returns `NaN` for every array.

An empty array divides by zero (`0 / 0` → `NaN`). `null`, `undefined`, or a non-array input throws when `.length` is read. Non-numeric elements also turn the sum into `NaN`.

raw.thought:
I am reviewing the JavaScript function to identify bugs.

The loop condition `i <= arr.length` causes an off-by-one error. It accesses `arr[arr.length]`, which is `undefined`, and adds it to the sum, producing `NaN`. An empty array also returns `NaN` because `0 / 0` evaluates to `NaN`.

The function also lacks input validation. Passing `null`, `undefined`, or a non-array value would throw a TypeError when accessing `.length`. Non-numeric elements in the array would likewise cause the sum to become `NaN`.

The off-by-one error is the primary bug. It causes the function to return NaN for any array, even non-empty ones.
